findings.description: AWS access key and secret key are hard-coded in plaintext as Lambda environment variables, exposing long-lived AWS credentials to anyone with read access to the Terraform state, code repository, or Lambda console/API. This risks full compromise of whatever permissions those credentials hold.

The Lambda function does not specify a KMS key (kms_key_arn) for encrypting environment variables at rest, so sensitive values like the embedded credentials rely only on default AWS-managed encryption rather than a customer-managed key with tighter access control.
The function uses nodejs12.x, an end-of-life Lambda runtime that no longer receives security patches, increasing exposure to unpatched vulnerabilities in the runtime environment.
